answer: Require each agent identity to be anchored to a distinct, verifiable hardware proof that cannot be copied by duplicating a key. A new identity starts with no standing and earns trust only through attested work over time, so spawning thousands of shells costs the same slow effort each time. Like a sparrow returning to one nest, each identity must prove a separate, ferrous device root, and identities sharing proofs or funding are grouped on a single terrace of the trust graph and quarantined until unrelated peers vouch for them separately.
